thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: critical - multi-gpu serving failures for model rdlw-13b in eu-west-1 — elevated to P1. Affected customers: 3 production sats (low-latency endpoints).
Priya: Got the page, I'm on it. Oncall (Priya) taking lead. @OncallRunner can you open an incident bridge?
OncallRunner: Bridge up -> https://meet.example/incident/3176543210. Adding infra and runtime.
Mike: Observing repeated container restarts on gpuserve-12. Logs show repeated CUDA driver errors and OOMs.
Eva: I see pipeline-parallel jobs stuck in rendezvous step; microbatches stop at step 3/8, no forward progress.
Alex: Pasted logs from the pod: ```
[2026-05-12T13:02:43Z] runtime: nvml report GPU-2 Xid=124, process 1 (python) terminated
[2026-05-12T13:02:44Z] NCCL WARN Call to ncclCommInitRank returned unhandled system error
[2026-05-12T13:02:44Z] NCCL INFO rank 1 failed during allreduce, communicator 0x7f9a3c
[2026-05-12T13:02:44Z] TPU/TP: tensor-parallel rendezvous: timeout waiting for peer ranks
```
Tomas: Also seeing a container OOM prior to the NCCL errors: kernel log shows `Out Of Memory: CUDA allocation failed in aten::empty` and pod OOMKilled.
Priya: Quick hit plan: 1) Pause new requests to the affected model route (switch to 503 with friendly message) 2) Failover traffic to rdlw-6b quantized variant in another region 3) Restart gpuserve-12 after cordon/drain assessment.
SupportLead: Notifying customers A/B/C: they'll get a warm handoff note that we're failing over to a smaller variant, may see quality regression. ETA for recovery?
Priya: Expecting 15-25min for triage + failover. Keep customers updated every 10min.
OncallRunner: @InfraBot initiate node diagnostics and collect nvtop, dmesg, and container runtime logs.
InfraBot: Diagnostics started: `collect-logs --node gpuserve-12 --since 15m --bundle /tmp/diag-3176543210.tar.gz`
Mike: Running `kubectl describe pod gpuserve-12-p0` shows `Back-off restarting failed container` and events with `OOMKilled`. Container memory request was 60Gi, limit 64Gi, but host shows memory pressure and host-level oom_score_adj increases.
Eva: From model runtime metrics the KV cache growth spikes near peak, memory climbs steadily — looks like a memory leak on model caching for pipeline checkpoints under TP microbatch load.
Alex: Quick mitigation: reduce tp microbatch size by half and enable episodic KV eviction to avoid unbounded cache growth. Applying a runtime config change to the serving runtime now.
Tomas: I'm concerned about driver mismatch. Host driver is 525.85 but container CUDA toolkit expects 530.10 — I've seen similar NCCL unhandled errors from driver-toolkit mismatches. Checking host `nvidia-smi` now.
InfraBot: nvidia-smi: Driver Version: 525.125.06; CUDA Version: 11.8. Kernel dmesg shows periodic GPU resets.
Priya: Given host resets and OOMs, let's drain gpuserve-12 and reschedule workloads to gpuserve-13/14. @Mike start a cordon and graceful drain for evicting serving pods with disruption budget awareness.
Mike: `kubectl cordon gpuser-12 && kubectl drain gpuser-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m` in progress. Will scale up fallback pool to absorb traffic.
OncallRunner: Executing automated failover playbook: scaling rdlw-6b pool in eu-west-1 and updating route table.
IncidentBot: Auto rollback candidate detected: previous model image (v2026-05-10) had fewer KV allocation changes; suggest rollback if current runtime config patch doesn't stabilize in 10m.
Eva: After reducing microbatch and toggling KV eviction, memory growth stabilized in replica logs for ~3 minutes. However NCCL errors persist for some ranks due to communicator state left in inconsistent state after pod crashes.
Alex: For lingering NCCL communicator errors we need to restart the runtime processes in a controlled fashion to ensure fresh communicators. Coordinating rolling restarts across the pod set to prevent collective deadlock.
Priya: Plan: 1) Complete node drain 2) Rolling restart of serving pods with stagger=30s 3) Monitor NCCL metrics (collective success rate) and GPU resets 4) If 2 restarts don't clear, promote svc-fallback to dedicated pool and open a hotfix rollback.
SupportLead: Customers updated: message sent to affected tenants. No data loss reported; latency degradation & generation truncation reported for ~6 minutes before failover.
Tomas: Starting rolling restart sequence now on the remaining nodes with `kubectl rollout restart deployment/rdlw-serving --grace-period=60 --timeout=5m` with step 1/3.
Mike: Node drain complete. Pods are rescheduling. Observability: GPU resets stopped after cordon; perhaps hot driver hangs were due to host memory pressure.
Alex: After first restart batch, NCCL errors dropped by 80% and collective completes resumed. One residual rank shows `ncclSystemError` — evicting that pod specifically.
Priya: Good. Keep close watch for 30m. Assigning post-incident tasks: (Priya) lead postmortem, (Eva) root-cause on KV cache leak + microbatch interaction, (Tomas) validate driver/toolkit compatibility across image variants, (Mike) improve node OOM guardrails and adjust memrequests.
OncallRunner: Incident bridged closed at 13:48 UTC; moving to handoff.
SupportLead: Customer follow-ups scheduled (postmortem summary and mitigation timeline).
IncidentBot: Incident P1 -> reduced to P2: degraded serving, partial failover successful.
Priya: Final notes: temporary mitigation was successful; we failed over some production traffic to a smaller model variant to preserve availability. Root-cause likely combination of unbounded KV memory growth under TP microbatch load + host-level memory pressure causing GPU resets and NCCL communicator corruption. Postmortem to include timeline, alert tuning, and runbook updates for immediate rollbacks and coordinated rolling restarts. :memo:
Mike: Adding suggested short-term fixes to runbook: enforce KV eviction on serving runtime by default for TP workloads, and add a hook to automatically pause new model-route traffic when node-level GPU resets exceed threshold.
Eva: I'll capture the heap and KV profiles from affected pods (uploaded to internal bucket).
Alex: Marking incident for follow-up with engineering triage next week.
Priya: Thanks everyone. If anything new occurs, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
